# Capability: playback

The contract of this folder is [`specs/playback/playback.md`](../../specs/playback/playback.md), `CAP-PLY`. Read it before a change
to what this capability does. A test title cites each criterion it verifies: `AC-PLY-###`.
The rules for all of `src/` are in [`src/AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md).

> Applies to `src/playback/**`, `src/spectrum/**`.

# Playback and spectrum

The engine is our own, on Web Audio, with no audio library. The reason for one value is in the
comment next to it. The decisions with a cost are four records:
[the engine](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-own-audio-engine.md),
[the lookahead](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-lookahead-scheduler.md),
[the cycle boundary](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-swap-at-the-cycle-boundary.md)
and [the click](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-click-is-a-fixed-pitch-bell.md).

## Rules

- **`voice.ts` and `scheduler.ts` do not import `engine.ts`.** They receive the audio context and
  the time as parameters, so a test renders them with an `OfflineAudioContext`. Only the import
  graph holds this: no lint rule does.
- **A decision goes where a `node` test reaches it.** Only the browser project runs `engine.ts`.
  Put the arithmetic in `scheduler.ts`, `playhead-offset.ts` or `spectrum-bars.ts`, and a value
  that a `node` test reads too. `engine.ts` keeps the wiring.
- **The engine speaks MIDI numbers, intervals and seconds.** `voice.ts`, `scheduler.ts` and
  `engine.ts` import no type of the board. Only `engine-bridge.ts` and `route-source.ts` know the
  sequence of the circuit.
- **What reaches the engine is what sounds.** A sequence carries no condition for the engine to
  evaluate. The click switch is the one exception: it is a switch of the mix, and it stays outside
  the sequence.
- **Only `use-engine.ts` moves the transport and queues a sequence.** One effect gives the same
  sequence to the engine and to `route-source.ts`. A second derivation can draw one circuit and
  play another, and no test fails.
- **The engine fails soft, so each caller asks what happened.** With no audio, `audio()` gives
  `null` and `startClock` does nothing, with no error. Read `clockRunning()` after a start, and
  show that answer (`BR-PLY-002`).

## Traps

- **Sound needs a user gesture.** The browser resumes the audio context only inside a handler
  that a gesture started. `playNow` and `startClock` resume it. A sound from a timer, an effect or
  a hover stays silent until the first click. A function that a frame loop calls reads `ctx`, not
  `audio()`, which would create the context with no gesture.
- **Each place that moves `origin` leaves `scheduledUntil` strictly before it.** If not, the first
  event of the cycle is lost, with no error. `startClock` and the two branches of the swap do it.
  For the swap at the cycle boundary, no test fails when the line is removed.
- **Two paths expand an arpeggio:** `playNotes` and `collectHits`. `DEFAULT_VOICE` and
  `intervalDuration` reach both. A change to how one path expands does not reach the other.
- **The default of the click switch lives twice:** the `useState` of `src/App.tsx` and
  `clicksAudible` in `engine.ts`. Change both.

## Verify the audio without hearing it

- **In a test,** render with the helpers of `src/playback/__tests__/test-context.ts`.
- **In the browser,** use the console of the dev server. The import gives the module of the app:

  ```js
  const m = await import('/src/playback/engine.ts');
  m.audio().state;    // 'running' after the first gesture
  m.clockRunning();   // the transport
  m.sequenceInfo();   // the sounding sequence: steps, clicks, crosses, length
  m.readSpectrum();   // null with no signal, else 128 bins
  ```

- **To prove that the scheduler fires,** wrap `createOscillator` of `m.audio()` with a counter.
  Each note, each crossing and each audible click makes one oscillator.
